_doc: THE ONE PLACE THE COLLEGE'S PHYSICAL SCHEMA IS NAMED.
Everything that needs to reach a college table - the SQL agent's prompt and
table allowlist, schema introspection, the read-only grants, the sync
worker's subscriptions, and the deterministic fast path - resolves names
through this file. Nothing else may contain a literal college table name.
WHY: the real college schema is not known yet. The current names are the
demo shape. When the real names arrive, adapting the system is editing this
file and re-running the suite, rather than auditing 15k lines for string
literals. That is the whole point, and it is why 'just rename the tables'
is not an acceptable substitute.
TODAY this maps every logical name to an IDENTICAL physical name, so the
system behaves exactly as it did before the adapter existed. A test asserts
that the derived allowlist equals the previous hardcoded list, so the
adapter cannot silently widen or narrow what the model can read.
FIELDS
schema   - the owning schema. 'public' on Postgres, 'dbo' on SQL Server.
physical - the physical table name in the college database.
columns  - logical column name -> physical column name. Only columns that
code refers to BY NAME need an entry; introspection discovers
the rest. Empty today because the current code refers to no
college column by literal name outside generated SQL.
SECURITY: this file is an ALLOWLIST. A table absent from it is unreachable
by the SQL agent. Adding an entry widens what the language model can read,
so additions are a security decision, not a configuration tweak. The
deliberately-absent tables are listed at the bottom under _excluded.
Tables the college database contains that this system must NOT read.
Recorded here so the exclusion is a visible decision with a reason,
rather than an absence somebody later reads as an oversight and 'fixes'.
These names are never resolved and never reach the allowlist.
_excluded.students: personal records; the assistant answers about the institution, not about individuals
_excluded.enrollments: identifies a named student with a named course
